harness: fresh general-purpose subagent, no inherited conversation context

completed.notes: BOTH faces, and it went further than any prior run: verified the host is POPULATED (4 entities, 1 PrimaryPlayer, 69 components) and then that it is a GAME — the body falls, lands on the authored floor with vel.y==0, walks 64->462 under drive_control_frame, jumps, lands on a ledge. 3/3 of its own tests green.

first_engine_file_reason: The cargo FEATURE list. docs/sdk/README.md's manifest section covers the bevy_ggrs patch and says nothing about the facade's ~30 features. Not an API question — a packaging one, same class as run 1's Cargo.lock.

the character-roster RON schema — the one place it could not proceed from docs
the name of the player marker component

compared_to_baseline.first_file_opened: Cargo.lock (cannot compile) -> ambition_world/src/lib.rs (cannot find a type) -> ambition/Cargo.toml (cannot find the feature list)
compared_to_baseline.reading: Three runs, three different first files, each a smaller question than the last: cannot build it, cannot find one type, cannot find the feature list. §4.2 still fails — the gate is ZERO.

findings.severity: highest — the docs tell third parties to copy this file
findings.summary: `Block::solid(name, MIN, size)` takes a min corner; fixtures/minimal_game passed a CENTRE, so the floor sat at x 320..960 in a 640-wide room while the walker spawned at x=64. The walker fell past it, blast-died, respawned, and fell again — forever — at a steady `Running { prepared: true }`.
findings.why_it_matters: ELEVEN tests were green on that game. Every one asked `host_status`, which answers 'did the engine start' and was answering it correctly. 'Is the game playable' is a different question and needs a position, settling. A suite that only asks the engine about itself passes over any amount of broken content.
findings.fix: Geometry corrected; `the_walker_lands_on_the_floor_instead_of_falling_through_it` asserts the body settles within 2px over 50 ticks. Seen red against the original geometry (y ranged 256..546).

findings.summary: §5 listed `ambition::experience` holding GameModule/ModuleManifest/ModuleDraft. They are in `ambition::app`. §5 is framed as an OUTPUT read off the call sites, which makes it the most trustworthy list in the SDK.
+y down, min-corner blocks, AuthoredWorld::new argument order — all derived by printing positions over 300 ticks. Now in the README.
`playable()` is what registers the gameplay route and `no_audio()` is effectively mandatory; the four-line snippet showed neither, so following it produces a host stuck in Activating.
PrimaryPlayer, BodyKinematics, drive_control_frame, ControlFrame — none in the prelude, none in docs/sdk/. Found by trawling rustdoc and the fixture's tests. Now a README section.

EMPTY_CHARACTER_ROSTER_RON solved the case nobody needs. Brute-forcing the non-empty case costs one build per missing field and DEAD-ENDS at the first enum-typed field (`tier`), because variant names cannot be guessed. The README's remedy is 'copy the fixture' — i.e. the documented fix for the leak is to open an engine file.
~30 facade features, none documented; the feature list was the first engine file this run opened.

what_worked: Build-time refusals: 'starts as character `blind_hero`, which no declared roster contains ... Characters available: none — the declared roster is empty'. The agent credits these with the run taking hours not days.
The patch-table warning saved the GgrsFrameTiming dead end entirely — blind run 1's top finding, closed, confirmed closed twice.
It reached a PLAYING game: fall, land, walk, jump, land.
verdict: Best run yet and the one that found the worst bug — in the fixture the SDK tells people to copy, invisible to eleven passing tests.
